name: Belgium (Gaming Commission) Market Profile

regulator.name: Kansspelcommissie / Commission des jeux de hasard

bindingStandards.name: Gaming Act of 7 May 1999 and Royal Decrees, including the RD on online games of chance and the amended RD on advertising and age

otherProhibitions.notes: From September 2024. If confirmed, this removes the entire bonus and free-spin promotional layer, which affects both product design and commercial modelling.

defaultDepositLimit.value: EUR 200 per week per operator by default, raisable only after checks including the National Bank credit register
defaultDepositLimit.notes: A credit-register check as a precondition for raising a limit is an unusual integration requirement.

selfExclusion.notes: Mandatory pre-play check. NOTE: "EPA" is not the Belgian register name.

minimumAge.notes: 21 for casino-type games and slots, raised from 18 in September 2024. The national lottery remains 18. Belgium is a notable European outlier - do not hardcode 18.

requirement.notes: Belgium has historically required online gaming servers in Belgium linked to a land-based licence (the .be co-location model). Current status must be confirmed; if it still applies it is a major architectural constraint.

recentChanges.change: Minimum age raised to 21 for casino-type games; bonus inducements banned
Radio advertising ban; GGR fell 4.86% to EUR 1.61bn in 2024, land-based down 7.59%

verificationRequired: Whether the .be server co-location requirement still applies - highest priority, architectural
Confirmation of the bonus inducement ban and its exact scope
Minimum age 21 confirmed against the Royal Decree
The default EUR 200 weekly deposit limit and the credit-register check mechanism
Minimum RTP, audit retention, accepted laboratories
consultantNotes: Belgium is commercially difficult for reasons unrelated to game design: age 21, a possible total bonus ban, a low default deposit limit, and a possible in-country server requirement tied to a land-based licence.
Almost everything here is MEDIUM or UNVERIFIED. A Belgian engagement should start with local counsel rather than with product configuration.
